problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{x+1}{(x+5)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x+5}+\frac{B}{(x+5)^{2}},
$$

find the real constants $A$ and $B.$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x+5)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & =A(x+5)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=-5$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-5+1 & =A(-5+5)+B \\ B & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ and using our value for $B$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0+1 & =A(0+5)-4 \\ 1 & =5A-4 \\ 5 & =5A \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $A=1$ and $B=-4.$
